GroupTrack V2.6c User Manual
Drill-down edition · device screenshots · 2026-06-23
Organized the way you navigate the app. Open a map to see its launch points; open a launch point to see its options; drill into an option to reach a single screen. Opening one branch collapses the others, so you always see just where you are.
Convoy Map
Every lettered control on the Convoy map toolbar. Open a launch point below to drill into it.
A — GroupTrack → Radio Setup
GroupTrack menu
Convoy Map › GroupTrack icon (Meshtastic left sidebar)

Tap the GroupTrack icon in the Meshtastic left-hand sidebar (the last icon) to open the GroupTrack menu — a slide-up panel. This is the entry to radio setup, the prerequisite for using GroupTrack with your Meshtastic radios.

The menu has two sections:

  • Event / Ride — the ride and radio options (expand to see them). covered below
  • Map Settings — an older submenu of map instructions, now built into the map panel itself. no longer used

Tap Event / Ride to expand it (next screen).

Setup Radio5 screens
Event / Ride menu
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride

Expanding Event / Ride reveals five options. In V2.5 only the two radio functions are used — ride creation and sharing are moving to the Release 3.0 cloud app.

  • Create a Ride coming in 3.0
  • Transfer Event/Ride Details via Email — “select a ride and send via email attachment” coming in 3.0
  • Import Ride from Downloads — “scan Downloads for .convoy files and import” coming in 3.0
  • Apply Ride Info to Radio — “apply master config or ride to connected radio.” used — see below
  • Restore Prior Config Post Ride — “select and restore from saved archive.” used — see below

Tap Apply Ride Info to Radio to begin applying config to a connected radio (next screen).

Apply Radio Config
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio

This screen applies a configuration to the connected radio so it reports each cart’s location to the Convoy map. The bar at the top shows the connection state — here ● CONNECTED, with the radio model (tracker-t1000-e) and firmware version. A radio must be connected before a config can be applied.

  • Apply Master Config — applies your saved master template to the connected radio. This is the function used in V2.5 to set a radio up for a ride. used
  • Apply Ride — applies a specific ride’s config. coming in 3.0
  • Review Changes → — shows what will change on the radio before you commit.

Tap Apply Master Config, then Review Changes to proceed (next screen).

Review — Changes to be Applied
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review

The review panel shows exactly what will be written to the radio before you commit. At the top, Long Name lets you set a name for the radio (here “Mike McKinney”) — edit it if you want this radio to carry a specific rider/cart name. Below, the New Channel (here Convoy, AES-256 encrypted) is the channel the radio will join.

The change table (Field · Current · New Value · Rule) is grouped into accordions you can expand to inspect each setting and see where its value is derived from:

  • LoRa — radio/region + modem settings
  • Channel — channel name, key, encryption
  • Device — device role and behavior
  • Position — GPS / position reporting
  • Display — on-radio display settings
  • Modules — module settings (telemetry, etc.)

Scrolling to the bottom of the panel shows the full accordion list and the action bar:

The action bar has two buttons: Cancel (red) backs out without changing the radio, and Proceed to Update (green) writes the config. Tap Proceed to Update to apply (next screen).

Reconnect Check
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review › Proceed to Update

After you proceed, the config is written and the radio reboots. This screen runs a 60-second countdown while the update is applied and the radio reconnects — the radio reboots, Bluetooth auto-disconnects, then auto-reconnects (shown in the log: “waiting for binary install reboot,” “auto BT disconnect,” “auto BT reconnect”). Let it run; Cancel stops the wait if needed.

When the countdown finishes, an update-apply recap is shown summarizing what was applied. Check the recap: if any settings did not apply correctly, simply reapply the update (return to Apply Master Config and proceed again).

Verify Config (apply recap)
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › … › Reconnect Check › Verify

After the reconnect, the app reads the radio back and compares every field against what it tried to write — only errors are shown. The header reports the result, e.g. “5 of 40 fields failed.” A group summary at the bottom shows pass/fail per category (Device, LoRa, Channel, Position, Display, Module).

In this example all five failures are in the Position group (Position 1/6) — the table lists each failed field with its Expected vs Actual value (e.g. Broadcast Interval expected 5, actual 0).

If any fields failed, reapply the update — go back to Apply Master Config and proceed again. Radios sometimes need a second pass for a group (often Position) to take. Re-verify until the recap shows all fields passed.

Restore Radio3 screens
Archive Restore
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride

A key GroupTrack safety feature: before it writes any configuration to a radio, it first saves that radio’s current config to a timestamped archive. Nothing you apply is ever destructive — the prior state is always recoverable. This screen lists the saved archives for the connected radio so you can restore any of them at any time.

The header shows the radio node and how many archives were found. Each entry is a saved config with its date and time and filename — note the pre_master suffix here, which is the config that was auto-saved just before the master config was applied. The size (e.g. 391b) is shown at right.

Tap an archive to restore it to the radio. Restore writes the saved config back and runs the same reconnect + verify sequence as Apply, so the radio reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified.

Restore — confirm (gated)
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › select archive

Selecting an archive highlights it (blue, with a check) and reveals a confirmation gate before anything is written. The warning makes the consequences explicit:

  • ⚠ Restore will overwrite current radio config — the selected archive replaces whatever is on the radio now.
  • Selected: the archive’s date/time, so you confirm you picked the right one.
  • Radio will reboot after restore.

Tap ↻ Restore This Archive to proceed. The radio then reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified — the same reconnect + verify sequence shown for Apply (above).

Restore — write & reconnect
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › Restore This Archive

After you confirm, Restore writes the archived config to the radio and runs the same write · reconnect · verify process documented under Apply (the 60-second Reconnect Check, then the Verify recap). When the recap shows all fields passed, the radio is back on the chosen prior configuration.

✓ This completes Convoy launch point A — GroupTrack / Radio Setup.

B — REC (record ride track)
Recording in progress
Convoy Map › REC

The REC button starts track recording for the ride. It works two ways depending on your setup: with no radios it records a track for just this cart (this device’s GPS path); with radio-equipped carts it activates group tracking for the whole convoy. Either way it creates and saves a track for the ride.

Tap REC and recording begins immediately — no prompt. The button changes to ❚❚ PAUSE, and a live Distance readout appears at the bottom-right and counts up as you move.

Tap Pause to interrupt recording (next screen).

Pause3 screens
Paused — End or continue
Convoy Map › REC › Pause

When you pause, recording holds and an End button appears below the Pause button. From here you choose:

  • Pause (top) — hold here; the button changes to Resume so you can continue when ready (see below).
  • End (below) — finish the recording and save the track.

Tap End to finish — you’ll be prompted to name the track (Save Track, below). Or, to continue the ride, the button shows Resume.

Resume
Convoy Map › REC › Pause › (continue)

If you don’t end, the recording stays paused and the button shows ▶ RESUME. Tap it to continue recording the same track from where you left off — the Distance readout picks back up. This lets you pause during stops and resume without starting a new track.

Save Track (name prompt)
Convoy Map › REC › Pause › End

Tapping End stops recording and opens the Save Track prompt. Type a Track name and tap Save to store the recorded track under that name. Skip discards the track (it is not saved). After saving, the REC button returns to its idle state.

The saved track becomes an artifact you can view, select, and export later from Work with Artifacts and from search.

C — Zoom (+/−)
Zoom
Convoy Map › Zoom (+/−)

The + and − buttons at the top-left zoom the map in and out. You can also pinch-to-zoom directly on the map. The current zoom level is shown in the header readout (e.g. N · Z13).

D — PLAN (launch Planning Map)
PLAN
Convoy Map › PLAN

The PLAN button switches from the Convoy (live) map to the Planning Map, where you search, download tiles, build routes, and manage artifacts. See Planning Map for everything you can do there. Use BACK on the Planning map to return to the Convoy map.

E — GROUP (whole group + group HUD)
GROUP display + HUD
Convoy Map › GROUP

GROUP shows the entire ride group on the map and displays the group heads-up display (HUD) at the bottom-left. It’s one of the bottom-bar view modes (GROUP · MY CART · SELECT CART · HIDE).

The group HUD reports the whole convoy at a glance:

  • Span — the distance from the lead cart to the tail cart (how spread out the group is).
  • Carts — total carts in the group.
  • Active — carts currently reporting.
  • Lost — carts not heard from within the set time window. (The active threshold and the “lost” minutes are both set in setup.)
  • △ Lead / ▽ Tail — the front and rear carts, with distance.
  • CH% — mesh channel utilization. Radios broadcast position every 5 seconds; if CH% turns red the channel is too busy — slow the broadcast frequency (slide the broadcast interval up) to reduce congestion.
F — MY CART (my cart + my HUD)
MY CART display + HUD
Convoy Map › MY CART

MY CART centers the map on your own cart (the starred marker, labeled with your cart name) and shows your cart’s heads-up display — your telemetry plus where you sit within the convoy.

The my-cart HUD shows:

  • Cart name — your cart’s name (e.g. “Fred & June”).
  • Heading — your direction of travel.
  • Battery — your device/radio battery level.
  • Altitude — your elevation.
  • Speed — your current speed.
  • To Lead / To Tail — your distance to the lead cart and to the tail cart.
  • Gap Ahead / Gap Behind — the gap to the cart immediately ahead of and behind you.
G — SELECT CART (detail on selected cart)
SELECT CART
Convoy Map › SELECT CART

SELECT CART opens a list of the carts in the group at the top of the screen. Tap the cart you want to view — the map centers on that cart and its heads-up display appears at the bottom-left. The cart currently being viewed is marked CURRENT in the list.

The selected-cart HUD shows the same details as MY CART, but for the chosen cart: Heading, Battery, Altitude, Speed, To Lead / To Tail, and Gap Ahead / Gap Behind. This lets you check any cart in the convoy, not just your own.

(pick a cart)1 screen
Selected cart — detail & actions
Convoy Map › SELECT CART › (pick a cart)

With a cart selected, its detail panel shows its live status and two action buttons. The detail fields include Status (Active), Spd (speed), Bat (battery), Pos # (its position/order in the convoy), Hdg (heading), Alt (altitude), and Seen (time since its last report).

  • Set as Lead — designate this cart as the lead cart for the ride.
  • Remove from Ride — remove this cart from the group. Use this when a cart is no longer part of the ride (breakdown, left early, etc.). Removing a cart stops “lost” messages for it and keeps the group span and stats accurate to the active riders only — so the GROUP view’s span no longer stretches out to a cart that has dropped off.
H — HIDE (clear the HUD)
HIDE
Convoy Map › HIDE

HIDE clears the heads-up display from the map for a clean, unobstructed view. The cart markers stay on the map and the Distance readout remains, but the detailed HUD block is removed. Tap any of the other modes (GROUP, MY CART, or SELECT CART) to bring the HUD back.

I — Settings gear (Convoy Settings)
Convoy Settings (panel 1)
Convoy Map › Settings gear

The gear opens Convoy Settings — a list of options that control the app’s behavior. This is where the thresholds referenced elsewhere in the manual are set.

  • Map Sources → Change Map Sources — assign tile sources to the SAT / TOPO / TOPO+ slots. (This is the one setting that opens its own screen — see below.)
  • Alert Thresholds → Signal Drop — minutes before the radio-disconnect warning fires (e.g. 2 min).
  • Signal Lost — minutes without a packet before a node is considered lost (e.g. 10 min). This is the “lost” window reflected in the group HUD’s Lost count.
  • Off Track — miles from the convoy track before the off-route alert fires (e.g. 0.5 mi).
  • Node Filter — admission settings for which nodes join the group (continues on panel 2).
(scroll down)1 screen
Convoy Settings (panel 2)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › (scroll down)

Scrolling down reveals the rest of Convoy Settings:

  • Node Filter → Admission Window — a node must have been heard within this window today to appear on the map (e.g. 1 hr).
  • Track Display → Multicolor Track — when on, the track is colored by node position.
  • Track Recording → Lead Cart Only — record the lead cart’s track only.
  • Track Recording Format — KML / GPX — the saved track format (GPX works with Garmin, Strava, AllTrails).
  • Removed Carts — lists carts you removed from the ride today (via SELECT CART → Remove from Ride); shows “No carts removed today” when none.

The app version and build are shown at the bottom of this screen.

Change Map Sources3 screens
Map Sources (drill-down)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › Change Map Sources

This is the one Convoy Settings option that opens its own screen. Map Sources assigns a tile source to each of the three fixed map slots used by the SAT / TOPO / TOPO+ buttons on the map toolbar.

  • SAT — the satellite slot (e.g. Esri Imagery + Roads + Labels).
  • TOPO — the topo slot (e.g. Esri World Topo).
  • TOPO+ — the detailed-topo slot (e.g. Esri USA Topo Maps).
  • Each slot has a Change button to pick a different source.
  • API Keys — some sources (e.g. Thunderforest Outdoors) require an API key; tap to enter the key to unlock them.

Tap Change on a slot to pick a new source (next screen).

Change source (picker)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › Change Map Sources › Change

Tapping Change opens a list of available tile sources, grouped by category. Tap a source to assign it to that slot; the currently-assigned source is checked.

  • Hybrid — imagery with roads/labels (Google Hybrid, Esri Imagery + Roads + Labels, USGS Imagery + Topo).
  • Satellite — plain imagery (Google Satellite, Esri World Imagery).
  • Topographic — topo maps (Esri USA Topo, Esri World Topo, OpenTopoMap, USGS Topo).
  • Street — road maps (Google Roads, OpenStreetMap, CartoDB Voyager).
  • Terrain — terrain maps (Google Terrain, and more).

Select a source and you return to the Map Sources screen with the slot updated (next screen).

Refresh Tiles (after a source change)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › Change Map Sources › Change › (select source)

After you assign a new source to a slot, the app offers to refresh the cached map tiles from the new source. It reports how many existing tiles it found and explains that the refresh downloads them at low priority, with progress visible in Work with Queues, and that it restarts automatically if interrupted.

  • Refresh Now — start re-downloading the tiles from the new source right away (low priority).
  • Later — keep the new source assignment but don’t refresh the cached tiles now.

✓ This completes Convoy launch point I — Settings (Convoy Settings → Map Sources → Change → Refresh).

J / K / L — SAT, TOPO, TOPO+ (map source buttons)
SAT · TOPO · TOPO+
Convoy Map › SAT / TOPO / TOPO+

These three toolbar buttons switch the displayed map source immediately. Each shows the source assigned to that slot in Convoy Settings → Map Sources (e.g. SAT = Esri Imagery, TOPO = Esri World Topo, TOPO+ = Esri USA Topo).

They work in either NET or LOCAL mode (see the NET/Local toggle). In local mode they display from tiles downloaded in advance — so you can switch sources and ride with no connection, as long as those map tiles were downloaded ahead of time.

M — NET / Local (network vs downloaded tiles)
NET / Local toggle
Convoy Map › NET / Local

This toggle switches between NET (network) and Local map modes:

  • NET — fetches map tiles live over the network (online).
  • Local — displays only from maps you have downloaded prior to your ride. If you haven’t downloaded the area in advance, local mode will have no maps to show — so download your ride area ahead of time to use it offline.
N — QUEUES (download queues)
Download Queues
Convoy Map › QUEUES

Queues opens the Download Queues panel, which manages map-tile downloads. The header shows the current state (e.g. “2 active, 1 queued”), and entries are grouped by status:

Segmented downloads: a large download area is automatically split into balanced segments — shown as 1/2, 2/2 and so on, each with its own tile count. The split keeps the segments close in size so the work is spread evenly, and each segment progresses independently. A download that stops partway can resume without restarting the segments that already finished.

  • Active — downloads in progress, each showing tiles downloaded and percent, with an X to cancel that entry.
  • Queued — downloads waiting to start (numbered #1, #2…), each with a timestamp and an X to remove it.
  • Completed — finished downloads, each listing the source (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+) and tile count.

Global controls: Hold pauses the queue, Cancel All stops everything, and Clear Done removes completed entries from the list. Close dismisses the panel.

O — Search (universal search)
Universal Search
Convoy Map › Search

The magnifying glass opens Universal Search — one search across five modes, shown as tabs: Area · Track · Route · Trail · Waypoint. Pick a tab, type in the field (the prompt changes per mode), and press Enter. There are two kinds of search:

  • Area — a place search. Type a place name (a town or a feature such as a park, e.g. “Bryce”) and the map repositions there. For common names, include the state to disambiguate — e.g. “Kanab, UT” — so it lands on the right place.
  • Track / Route / Trail / Waypoint — artifact searches. These search your saved and imported artifacts by name. The search presents a list of matching hits; select one and its artifact detail panel opens. From the detail panel, use FIT to center the map on it.

Example — Area search for “Panguitch, UT”: the map repositions to Panguitch and the trails and tracks for that area draw immediately.

Example — artifact search: searching a name returns a list of matching hits (here two results for “Panguitch”), each with its name and ID.

Selecting a hit opens that artifact’s detail panel:

The detail panel shows the artifact’s name and type, an Aliases field, and a Details section — including the Carto Type band, its ID and bounding box, and an expandable technical section. Down the left is the action column: Rename, Delete, Share, Export, and FIT. Tap FIT to center and frame the map on that one artifact. Close dismisses the panel.

After FIT the panel closes and the map zooms to frame that artifact — here the selected track centered and fit to the view:

In short: Area moves the map to a place; the artifact modes find a saved item by name and open its details (then FIT centers the map on it).

P — Work with Artifacts
Work with Artifacts panel
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts (hamburger)

The hamburger opens the Work with Artifacts panel, which controls the four artifact types — Tracks, Trails, Waypoints, Routes — on the map. Important: all of these controls operate on the bounding box of the current display — i.e. the artifacts within the area you’re currently viewing, not the whole database.

Each type row has three buttons (the highlighted one is the current state):

  • OFF — hide that artifact type on the map.
  • ALL — show all artifacts of that type within the current view.
  • SEL/EDIT — opens a list of that type’s artifacts in the current view for per-artifact control: Select All, Deselect All, or check a custom combination to choose exactly which are shown. (OFF and ALL are in-panel toggles; only SEL/EDIT opens a screen.)
SEL/EDIT1 screen
SEL/EDIT list (per-artifact)
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › SEL/EDIT

Tapping SEL/EDIT on a type opens its list — here Trails (23), all the trails in the current view. Each has a checkbox, with Select All and Deselect All at the top, so you can show every one, hide every one, or pick a custom mix.

You can also tap an artifact’s name in this list to open its detail info panel (the same panel shown under Search — name, type, Carto Type, IDs, with Rename / Delete / Share / Export / FIT). Tap FIT there to center that one artifact on screen.

✓ This completes Convoy launch point P — Work with Artifacts.

Q — ? (Help & Info)
Help & Info
Convoy Map › ?

The ? button opens Help & Info, with two choices:

  • Full Manual — opens the complete user manual, bundled in the app (a screen-by-screen cookbook with its own search box and contents).
  • Release Notes — opens the release notes for the current version.

Full Manual:

Release Notes — includes the important upgrade warning (install as an update, do not clean-install) and the “What’s new” list for the build:

Map gestures — tap artifact & long-press
Tap an artifact → popup
Convoy Map › tap an artifact

Tapping an artifact on the map (a trail, track, etc.) opens a quick-info popup with its name and key properties. This is the fast look-up; for the full detail panel, select the artifact’s name in a search result or a SEL/EDIT list instead.

The fields shown depend on the artifact type — each type (trail, track, route, waypoint) displays its own relevant data. A trail, for example, shows Type (e.g. “4 - Road-concurrent”), Surface, Uses, Motorized, Horse, and County; other types show their own fields. Tap the × to close the popup.

BACK
Planning Map › BACK

G — Work with Artifacts
Work with Artifacts panel
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts (hamburger)

The hamburger opens the Work with Artifacts panel, which controls the four artifact types — Tracks, Trails, Waypoints, Routes — on the map. Important: all of these controls operate on the bounding box of the current display — i.e. the artifacts within the area you’re currently viewing, not the whole database.

Each type row has three buttons (the highlighted one is the current state):

A + Route button at the top starts building a new route.

Planning-only: Import Trails & Import Artifacts
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts

The Planning version of this panel is the same as the Convoy one, plus two import buttons at the bottom:

  • Import Trails — brings in trails data from external trail resources (the trail-source databases).
  • Import Artifacts — imports artifacts from Gaia or onX files, so you can transfer your historical data (tracks, routes, waypoints) from those apps into GroupTrack.
SEL/EDIT1 screen
SEL/EDIT list (per-artifact)
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › SEL/EDIT

Tapping SEL/EDIT on a type opens its list — here Trails (23), all the trails in the current view. Each has a checkbox, with Select All and Deselect All at the top, so you can show every one, hide every one, or pick a custom mix.

You can also tap an artifact’s name in this list to open its detail info panel (the same panel shown under Search — name, type, Carto Type, IDs, with Rename / Delete / Share / Export / FIT). Tap FIT there to center that one artifact on screen.

+ Route4 screens
+ Route — start a route
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route

Before you start: zoom into the area where you want to build the route. It helps to display Trails and Tracks (turn them on in Work with Artifacts) as a visual guide — the snap-to function works over both tracks and trails, so your route follows a known track or trail wherever one is available, keeping it on established paths.

Tapping + Route opens the Start a route dialog:

  • New Route — start building a new route straight away. You are not asked for a name here — the route is saved automatically as you build, and you name it when you tap Save.
  • In Progress — resume an unfinished route you started earlier.

The only difference is whether you start a fresh route or resume one already in progress. Choose New Route to begin building (next screen). Because every point is saved as you go, a route left unfinished can always be picked up again from In Progress.

Building the route
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route › New Route

The Route panel opens for building. Tap the map to place points — the route draws as a pink line, and each new point adds length and snaps to a nearby trail/track when one is available, keeping the route on known paths.

The panel controls:

  • Method — Point (live; tap to place points). Draw and Suggest are marked “soon.”
  • Build (n pts) — shows how many points the route has so far.
  • Add ON — toggles point-adding on/off as you tap.
  • Undo — removes the last point.
  • Save — saves the finished route.
  • Discard — abandons the route without saving.

Keep tapping to extend the route; each point snaps to the underlying track/trail.

Extending & saving the route
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route › (building)

As you keep tapping, the route grows and the Build point count climbs (here 20 points). The pink route traces the chosen path, snapped to the underlying tracks/trails.

When you tap Save, you can save the route as a work in progress (to resume and finish later via + Route → In Progress) or as a completed route.

Save route
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route › Save

The Save route dialog offers two ways to save:

  • Save as in progress — keep editing later; resume it via + Route → In Progress.
  • Save as completed route — graduate it to a finished, saved route (then searchable and listed like any other artifact).

✓ This completes Convoy launch point G — Work with Artifacts.

Import Trails1 screen
Import Trails → Select Source
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › Import Trails

Import Trails opens a Select Source list of approved external trail sources. Each entry shows its type, scope, and trail count (e.g. UGRC Utah Trails, Arizona State Parks & Trails, Colorado COTREX, BLM, USFS, USGS National Trails, NPS Public Trails). Sources you’ve already brought in are marked IMPORTED.

Select a source and tap VALIDATE to import it. The import process runs and reports how many trails were processed and how many were added. (BACK returns without importing.)

Import Artifacts1 screen
Import Artifacts (from Gaia / onX GPX)
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › Import Artifacts

Import Artifacts migrates your historical data from Gaia, onX, or similar apps into GroupTrack. The workflow:

  1. First (outside GroupTrack): in your current app, export/download the artifacts you want as GPX files, and move them into your device’s Downloads directory.
  2. Run Import Artifacts — GroupTrack scans Downloads and lists the GPX/KML files it finds.
  3. Check the file(s) you want (or Select All), then tap Select files to import.
  4. The import runs, bringing those artifacts into GroupTrack. On completion the GPX files are removed from Downloads.

The screen header shows how many files were found; each entry lists its name, size, date, and format. A RESYNC TRACKS button is also here — the same one referenced in the upgrade notes for bringing recorded tracks back after an update.

H — ? (Help & Info)
Help & Info
Planning Map › ?

The ? button opens Help & Info, with two choices:

  • Full Manual — opens the complete user manual, bundled in the app (a screen-by-screen cookbook with its own search box and contents).
  • Release Notes — opens the release notes for the current version.

Full Manual:

Release Notes — includes the important upgrade warning (install as an update, do not clean-install) and the “What’s new” list for the build:

I — KEY (map legend)
KEY / Legend
Planning Map › KEY

The KEY button (bottom-left) opens the map Legend popup, which explains the color of every line on the map. Tap the × to close it.

  • OHV / Road — blue
  • Hiking & Biking — orange
  • Hiking Only — yellow
  • Biking Only — purple
  • Paved / other — cyan
  • Track — green
  • Route — magenta
  • Waypoint — green marker

The legend is on the Planning map; the Convoy map does not show it.

J — Downloads (tiles & artifacts)
Downloads panel
Planning Map › Downloads (bottom-right)

The Downloads button (bottom-right) opens the Downloads panel — where you set up and start downloads of map tiles and artifacts for offline use. This is different from Queues: Downloads is where you initiate a download (pick an area and what to grab); Queues shows the status/progress of downloads already running.

  • Local toggle — switch the map to local (downloaded) tiles.
  • Map Controls — download-related map options.
  • Select Tiles / Artifacts — choose what to download (map tiles and/or artifacts).
  • Draw Area — draw a region on the map to define the download extent.
  • Show Downloads — see what has been downloaded.
  • Refresh Downloads — re-fetch / update downloaded data.
Map Controls1 screen
Downloads → Map Controls
Planning Map › Downloads › Map Controls

Expanding Map Controls sets the two parameters that define a download’s extent and detail:

  • Flyover (Mileage) — sets the range of the Area search: how far out from the center the map radius extends (e.g. 0.0 mi). A larger value covers a wider area around the search center.
  • Zoom — the maximum zoom level that gets downloaded (e.g. Z18). Higher zoom = more detailed tiles (and more data).
Select Tiles / Artifacts1 screen
Downloads → Select Tiles / Artifacts
Planning Map › Downloads › Select Tiles / Artifacts

This section specifies the target of the download — what to act on for the drawn bounding box. Three functions are available now:

  • Download Tiles — download map tiles for the drawn bounding box.
  • Import Trails — download trail sources for the bounding box (all trails for that area, regardless of source).
  • Remove Tiles — remove downloaded tiles from the system for the bounding box area.

Waypoints, Tracks, and Routes are shown greyed out and tagged V2.6 — those download targets are coming in a later release.

Draw Area2 screens
Downloads → Draw Area
Planning Map › Downloads › Draw Area

Draw Area defines the bounding box that the download targets (Download Tiles / Import Trails / Remove Tiles) act on. Expand the Draw Area accordion, then tap Draw Area and use your finger to outline the region of the map you want to select.

  • Draw Area — start drawing; trace the area on the map with your finger.
  • Clear — remove the drawn area and start over.
Downloads → drawing & starting the download
Planning Map › Downloads › Draw Area › (outline)

The full flow: first check what you want to download (e.g. Download Tiles), then draw your box. The outline appears in orange. When you lift your finger, the panel shows the area’s coordinates and an estimate (e.g. “~1366 tiles · 20 MB”), and a Download Selected button appears.

Press Download Selected and the download begins — you can watch its progress in Queues. Use the tile/size estimate to gauge how big the download will be before committing.

Show Downloads1 screen
Downloads → Show Downloads
Planning Map › Downloads › Show Downloads

Show Downloads overlays your tile coverage on the map as shaded areas, so you can see at a glance what you have offline:

  • Downloaded maps area (blue) — areas already downloaded on the device.
  • Maps in queue (red) — areas selected and waiting in the download queue.

Each checkbox toggles its overlay on or off. This is a quick way to confirm your ride area is covered offline before you head out.

K — Tap an artifact (popup)
Tap an artifact → popup
Planning Map › tap an artifact

Tapping an artifact on the map opens a quick-info popup with its name and key properties. The fields shown depend on the artifact type — each type (trail, track, route, waypoint) displays its own relevant data. This is the fast look-up; for the full detail panel, select the artifact’s name in a search result or a SEL/EDIT list instead.

A trail popup, for example, shows Type, Surface, Uses, Motorized, Horse, and County. Tap the × to close it. (Same behavior as the Convoy map.)

L — GroupTrack → Radio Setup
GroupTrack menu
Planning Map › GroupTrack icon (Meshtastic left sidebar)

Tap the GroupTrack icon in the Meshtastic left-hand sidebar (the last icon) to open the GroupTrack menu — a slide-up panel. This is the entry to radio setup, the prerequisite for using GroupTrack with your Meshtastic radios.

The menu has two sections:

  • Event / Ride — the ride and radio options (expand to see them). covered below
  • Map Settings — an older submenu of map instructions, now built into the map panel itself. no longer used

Tap Event / Ride to expand it (next screen).

Setup Radio5 screens
Event / Ride menu
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride

Expanding Event / Ride reveals five options. In V2.5 only the two radio functions are used — ride creation and sharing are moving to the Release 3.0 cloud app.

  • Create a Ride coming in 3.0
  • Transfer Event/Ride Details via Email — “select a ride and send via email attachment” coming in 3.0
  • Import Ride from Downloads — “scan Downloads for .convoy files and import” coming in 3.0
  • Apply Ride Info to Radio — “apply master config or ride to connected radio.” used — see below
  • Restore Prior Config Post Ride — “select and restore from saved archive.” used — see below

Tap Apply Ride Info to Radio to begin applying config to a connected radio (next screen).

Apply Radio Config
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio

This screen applies a configuration to the connected radio so it reports each cart’s location to the Convoy map. The bar at the top shows the connection state — here ● CONNECTED, with the radio model (tracker-t1000-e) and firmware version. A radio must be connected before a config can be applied.

  • Apply Master Config — applies your saved master template to the connected radio. This is the function used in V2.5 to set a radio up for a ride. used
  • Apply Ride — applies a specific ride’s config. coming in 3.0
  • Review Changes → — shows what will change on the radio before you commit.

Tap Apply Master Config, then Review Changes to proceed (next screen).

Review — Changes to be Applied
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review

The review panel shows exactly what will be written to the radio before you commit. At the top, Long Name lets you set a name for the radio (here “Mike McKinney”) — edit it if you want this radio to carry a specific rider/cart name. Below, the New Channel (here Convoy, AES-256 encrypted) is the channel the radio will join.

The change table (Field · Current · New Value · Rule) is grouped into accordions you can expand to inspect each setting and see where its value is derived from:

  • LoRa — radio/region + modem settings
  • Channel — channel name, key, encryption
  • Device — device role and behavior
  • Position — GPS / position reporting
  • Display — on-radio display settings
  • Modules — module settings (telemetry, etc.)

Scrolling to the bottom of the panel shows the full accordion list and the action bar:

The action bar has two buttons: Cancel (red) backs out without changing the radio, and Proceed to Update (green) writes the config. Tap Proceed to Update to apply (next screen).

Reconnect Check
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review › Proceed to Update

After you proceed, the config is written and the radio reboots. This screen runs a 60-second countdown while the update is applied and the radio reconnects — the radio reboots, Bluetooth auto-disconnects, then auto-reconnects (shown in the log: “waiting for binary install reboot,” “auto BT disconnect,” “auto BT reconnect”). Let it run; Cancel stops the wait if needed.

When the countdown finishes, an update-apply recap is shown summarizing what was applied. Check the recap: if any settings did not apply correctly, simply reapply the update (return to Apply Master Config and proceed again).

Verify Config (apply recap)
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › … › Reconnect Check › Verify

After the reconnect, the app reads the radio back and compares every field against what it tried to write — only errors are shown. The header reports the result, e.g. “5 of 40 fields failed.” A group summary at the bottom shows pass/fail per category (Device, LoRa, Channel, Position, Display, Module).

In this example all five failures are in the Position group (Position 1/6) — the table lists each failed field with its Expected vs Actual value (e.g. Broadcast Interval expected 5, actual 0).

If any fields failed, reapply the update — go back to Apply Master Config and proceed again. Radios sometimes need a second pass for a group (often Position) to take. Re-verify until the recap shows all fields passed.

Restore Radio3 screens
Archive Restore
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride

A key GroupTrack safety feature: before it writes any configuration to a radio, it first saves that radio’s current config to a timestamped archive. Nothing you apply is ever destructive — the prior state is always recoverable. This screen lists the saved archives for the connected radio so you can restore any of them at any time.

The header shows the radio node and how many archives were found. Each entry is a saved config with its date and time and filename — note the pre_master suffix here, which is the config that was auto-saved just before the master config was applied. The size (e.g. 391b) is shown at right.

Tap an archive to restore it to the radio. Restore writes the saved config back and runs the same reconnect + verify sequence as Apply, so the radio reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified.

Restore — confirm (gated)
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › select archive

Selecting an archive highlights it (blue, with a check) and reveals a confirmation gate before anything is written. The warning makes the consequences explicit:

  • ⚠ Restore will overwrite current radio config — the selected archive replaces whatever is on the radio now.
  • Selected: the archive’s date/time, so you confirm you picked the right one.
  • Radio will reboot after restore.

Tap ↻ Restore This Archive to proceed. The radio then reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified — the same reconnect + verify sequence shown for Apply (above).

Restore — write & reconnect
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › Restore This Archive

After you confirm, Restore writes the archived config to the radio and runs the same write · reconnect · verify process documented under Apply (the 60-second Reconnect Check, then the Verify recap). When the recap shows all fields passed, the radio is back on the chosen prior configuration.
